deep.reconstruction: Context: this is the Latin working material around Riemann's Paris prize memoir (Commentatio mathematica, 1861) on heat conduction: when can a family of isothermal surfaces stay isothermal in time in a homogeneous body, and what does that force on the metric ds^2 = sum b_{ii'} ds_i ds_i'. The page consists of four blocks. (1) Top, 'p. 8': the heat equation Delta u = du/dt is to be brought into the form (a): sum_nu p_nu dq_nu/dt = sum T(alpha,beta) Q(beta,t), where p_1..p_mu are mu particular solutions of 'equation 1' (not on this page) chosen with no identical linear relation sum g_nu p_nu = 0. Riemann then says that mu special values alpha_1..alpha_mu can be given to alpha so that the determinant sum +- p_1(alpha_1)...p_mu(alpha_mu) is nonzero (the standard fact that linearly independent functions admit a nonvanishing evaluation determinant). Substituting these values into (a) lets one express dq_nu/dt through derivatives of the q with respect to beta, free of alpha. This step is correct (my gloss: solve a linear system with an invertible matrix). (2) 'p. 12', formula I: the vanishing of the curvature tensor of the form with coefficients b: d2 b_{i i''}/ds_i' ds_i''' + d2 b_{i' i'''}/ds_i ds_i'' - d2 b_{i i'''}/ds_i' ds_i'' - d2 b_{i' i''}/ds_i ds_i''' + (1/2B) sum_{lambda,kappa} beta_{lambda kappa}(p_{lambda,i' i'''} p_{kappa,i i''} - p_{lambda,i' i''} p_{kappa,i i'''}) = 0, with B = det b, beta_{lambda kappa} the cofactors (so beta/B is the inverse metric) and p_{nu,i i'} = d b_{nu i}/ds_i' + d b_{nu i'}/ds_i - d b_{i i'}/ds_nu = 2 x (Christoffel symbol of the first kind). This is the condition that ds^2 is flat (twice the Riemann tensor R_{i i' i'' i'''} up to sign convention). (3) 'p. 12 in der Linie': three polarised relations for a geodesic (line): 2 sum b_{i nu} d^2 s_i = - sum p_{nu i i'} ds_i ds_i', and the same with d d s -> d delta s and delta delta s, i.e. the geodesic equation written with p. The left column (variations d, delta, delta' of the quadratic form) is hard to read and I do not reconstruct it. (4) 'p. 13': a note (in the first person plural, 'we have tried to restore in full the calculations needed to confirm these propositions') introduces Case I, m = 1, of the three-variable problem. The data is a 2 x 3 array (0 0 c / a' b' c'), which I read as the coefficients of a ternary quadratic form with diagonal (0,0,c) and cross coefficients (a', b', c'), i.e. 2a' dbeta dgamma + 2b' dalpha dgamma + 2c' dalpha dbeta + c dgamma^2 (my interpretation; a', b' are linear in gamma, c' independent of gamma). Its symmetric 3x3 determinant is 2a'b'c' - c c'^2 and must be constant. The adjoint form is -(a' dalpha + b' dbeta - c' dgamma)^2 + 2(2a'b' - c c') dalpha dbeta, and 2a'b' - cc' is then independent of gamma (since c' is and the determinant is constant). Riemann claims that a linear substitution in gamma brings this to (a dalpha + c dgamma)^2 + 2m dalpha dbeta with a linear in gamma and c, m independent of gamma ('facile perspicitur'; note the letters c, a are reused with new meaning). Next the conditions for this form to be equivalent to dx^2+dy^2+dz^2 (flatness) are derived. Metric coefficients: b_11 = a^2, b_13 = ac, b_33 = c^2, b_12 = m, b_22 = b_23 = 0. The list of p_{nu,i i'} (p_{1,11} = d(a^2)/dalpha, p_{1,22} = 2 dm/dbeta, p_{1,33} = 2 d(ac)/dgamma - d(c^2)/dalpha, p_{1,23} = d(ac)/dbeta, p_{1,31} = d(a^2)/dgamma, p_{1,12} = d(a^2)/dbeta; p_{2,11} = 2 dm/dalpha - d(a^2)/dbeta, p_{2,22} = 0, p_{2,33} = - d(c^2)/dbeta, p_{2,23} = 0, p_{2,31} = - d(ac)/dbeta, p_{2,12} = 0; p_{3,11} = 2 d(ac)/dalpha - d(a^2)/dgamma, p_{3,22} = p_{3,33} = 0, p_{3,23} = d(c^2)/dbeta, p_{3,31} = d(c^2)/dalpha, p_{3,12} = d(ac)/dbeta) is correct throughout (I recomputed it). Then the six flatness equations (ii', i''i''') = 0 are listed: (11) m c_bb - c_b m_b = 0; (22) mc(c_aa - a_ag) + (a_g - c_a)(c m_a + m a_g) = 0; (33), (23), (13) 2mc (ac)_bb - 2c (ac)_b m_b - 2m c_b (ac)_b = 0; (12) 2m(2c c_ab - (ac)_bg) + (c a_b - a c_b)^2 = 0. Below them are scratch lines: d/dbeta log((ac)_beta) = (c m_b + m c_b)/(mc) = d log(mc)/dbeta (follows from (13)), and the start of the case c = f(alpha+beta), m = f' treated on the next page: c_ab = f'', giving f f'' + 4 psi(alpha)^2 f'^2/f^2 ... and f^3 f''/f' = -psi(alpha)^2 (the final scratch line is garbled in the transcription: the image reads minus an alpha-function squared, presumably psi^2). I verified that (12) with a = psi/c, c = f(alpha+beta), m = f' does yield f^3 f''/f' = -psi^2. The page is thus an unpublished-in-this-form working sheet for the n = 3 classification of flat metrics admitting isothermal families, continued on the next folio.
errors: Equation (11), (22), (13) and (12) as written agree (up to a nonzero factor) with the sympy-computed components R_{23,23}, R_{13,13}, R_{12,23}, R_{13,23} of the curvature tensor of the metric a=a1+gamma*a2, c, m independent of gamma. So these four are correct.

Equations (33) and (23) as transcribed do NOT match the corresponding curvature components R_{12,12} and R_{12,13} in my sympy check (with either d2a/dbeta2 or d2(a^2)/dbeta2 in (33)). Since the hand is hard to read at the superscripts and the (ac)_beta terms, I cannot tell whether this is a transcription problem or a slip by the writer. Treat as unresolved.

The step 'facile perspicitur' (a linear change of gamma turns -(a' dalpha + b' dbeta - c' dgamma)^2 + 2(2a'b'-cc')dalpha dbeta into (a dalpha + c dgamma)^2 + 2m dalpha dbeta) is not justified on the page: a' and b' both depend on gamma and a change of gamma alone cannot remove the b' dbeta term; it also changes the overall sign of the square. Possibly more substitutions (in alpha, beta) or complex scaling are implied. Unverified.

Notation clash: the letters a, b, c appear first as a', b', c' (matrix entries), then c and a with new meaning in the reduced form, and in (11)-(13) 'a' stands for the reduced a; also gamma-derivatives are written d/dgamma inside equations in which c and m do not depend on gamma.

The first column of 'p. 12 in der Linie' relations (variations delta', delta, d) cannot be checked from the transcription; the signs in the first column look inconsistent between the three lines as transcribed.
The scratch line 'f^3 f''/f' = -4c' is presumably -psi(alpha)^2 (the next page has f'' f^3/f' = -psi(alpha)^2), so the '4' is probably a reading of the superscript.

results.what: Existence of mu values alpha_1..alpha_mu making the evaluation determinant of mu linearly independent functions nonzero, used to eliminate alpha from (a)
results.modern_name: Linear independence implies a nonvanishing generalised Wronskian/alternant determinant at suitable points (Gram/Haar-type lemma)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard linear algebra lemma, no single credit (19th century)

results.what: Formula I: vanishing of the Riemann curvature tensor of a quadratic differential form in terms of b_{ii'} and Christoffel symbols of the first kind p_{nu,ii'}
results.modern_name: Riemann curvature tensor / flatness condition R_{ijkl}=0
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Commentatio 1861, published 1876), also Christoffel and Lipschitz 1869

results.what: Geodesic equation 2 sum b_{i nu} d^2 s_i = - sum p_{nu ii'} ds_i ds_i' and its polarised forms
Case m=1 of the n=3 problem: reduction of the form to (a dalpha + c dgamma)^2 + 2m dalpha dbeta and computation of the first-kind Christoffel symbols p for it
results.modern_name: Classification of flat 3-metrics (Euclidean) with a one-parameter isothermal-type family; computation of Christoffel symbols for a metric in null-type coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's Commentatio (Paris prize) sketches the result; the detailed calculations are in the Nachlass edited by Weber/Dedekind

results.what: Flatness equations (11)-(12) for the metric (a dalpha + c dgamma)^2 + 2m dalpha dbeta with a linear in gamma, c and m independent of gamma
results.modern_name: Component equations of R_{ijkl}=0 for a specific ansatz

results.what: From (13): d log((ac)_beta)/dbeta = d log(mc)/dbeta, and from (12) with c=f(alpha+beta), m=f', a=psi/c the ODE f^3 f''/f' = -psi(alpha)^2
results.modern_name: Separation of variables in the flatness PDE system

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working sheet for the n=3 (m=1) case of the Commentatio mathematica: the curvature formula and geodesic equations are the known Riemannian content, and the rest is a detailed calculation whose results are already in the literature as part of the Nachlass edition. Nothing here suggests a result not already attributed to Riemann; the only mildly notable features are the explicit working of the Christoffel list and the unresolved inconsistent equations (33), (23).

checkable.asserts: The determinant of the symmetric matrix with diagonal (0,0,c) and cross entries c', b', a' is 2a'b'c' - c c'^2 (a1=a', b1=b', c1=c', c0=c).
The adjoint form is -(a' dalpha + b' dbeta - c' dgamma)^2 + 2(2a'b' - cc') dalpha dbeta.
